To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the facial wiping response of rat pups can be elicited by lemon juice in the absence of the usual environmental constraints, and that this response can be demonstrated as early as 19 days of gestational age.

the facial wiping response is present in fetuses but absent in pups in a standard postnatal environment, and that this response can be elicited in neonates by placing them in a preweaning environment.
the facial wiping response of the rat is present at 19 days of gestation and is not expressed in the neonatal period.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ontogeny and the phylogeny of species-typical behavior.
the appearance, disappearance and reappearance of species-typical action patterns during early development.
the ontogeny, or development over time, of a species-typic behavior, facial wiping, and with the role of environmental constraints in this development.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the wiping response of the rat is a species-typical response that is present in the repertoire of the fetus, disappears from the repertoire of the pup, and reappears in the repertoire of both the pup and adult in certain test situations.
the ontogeny, phylogeny, and function of facial wiping is still not fully understood.
the facial wiping response of rat pups is not an age-typical response.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, although the facial wiping response is not present in rat pups during the early postnatal period, this response can be elicited in the appropriate test situation.
, in the absence of environmental constraints, the facial wiping response appears, disappears, and reappears during early development.
, although facial wiping can be elicitted in the neonate in the absence of a typical elicitor, it is not a typical response of the rat neonate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the study of behavioral continuity between prenatal and postnatal periods is a complex endeavor that should be approached with caution.
the ontogeny and the development of a species-typic action pattern can be studied by examining the effects of the environment on the expression of that action pattern.
the study of behavioral continuity should not focus exclusively on the appearance of species-typical action patterns.
